explanation.title: Spanish Verbal Periphrases: Expressing Actions with Nuance

sections.subtitle: Progressive Forms (Estar + Gerund)
sections.content:
📋 Present Progressive

✅ Structure:
• estar (conjugated) + gerund (-ando/-iendo)

💡 Examples:
→ Estoy comiendo (I am eating)
→ Está hablando (He/She is talking)
→ Estaba estudiando (I was studying)
→ Estaré trabajando (I will be working)

⚡ Critical Difference from English:

Spanish present tense → habitual actions
→ Como a las 2 (I eat at 2 - habitual)

Progressive → RIGHT NOW actions
→ Estoy comiendo ahora (I'm eating now - in progress)

🎯 Uses:

1️⃣ Actions in progress at the moment

2️⃣ Temporary situations:
→ Estoy viviendo en Madrid
  (I'm living in Madrid temporarily)

📍 Reserve progressive for actions happening RIGHT NOW

sections.subtitle: Immediate Future & Recent Past
sections.content:
📋 Two Essential Constructions

✅ IR A + INFINITIVE (going to):

💡 Formation:
• ir (present) + a + infinitive

💡 Examples:
→ Voy a estudiar (I'm going to study)
→ ¿Vas a venir? (Are you going to come?)
→ Van a llegar tarde (They're going to arrive late)

🎯 Use: Express near future plans/intentions
📍 Most common way to express future in spoken Spanish

⚠️ ACABAR DE + INFINITIVE (just did):

💡 Formation:
• acabar (present) + de + infinitive

💡 Examples:
→ Acabo de comer (I just ate)
→ Acabamos de llegar (We just arrived)
→ Acaba de salir (He/She just left)
→ ¿Acabas de despertar? (Did you just wake up?)

🎯 Use: Express recent past actions
⚡ Use present tense of acabar for recent past!

sections.subtitle: Repeated Actions & Habit
sections.content:
📋 Expressing Repetition & Habit

✅ VOLVER A + INFINITIVE (to do again):

💡 Examples:
→ Vuelvo a intentar (I'm trying again)
→ Volvió a llamar (He called again)
→ No vuelvas a hacerlo (Don't do it again)

🎯 Use: Emphasize repetition

⚠️ SOLER + INFINITIVE (usually do):

💡 Examples:
→ Suelo desayunar a las 8
  (I usually have breakfast at 8)
→ Solía fumar (I used to smoke)

📋 Important Limitations:
• Only in present and imperfect tenses
• Cannot be used in other tenses

💡 Alternative for other tenses:
Use 'normalmente' or 'generalmente' with regular verb
→ Normalmente desayuno a las 8
→ Generalmente llegaba tarde

sections.subtitle: Beginning & Ending Actions
sections.content:
📋 Starting & Stopping Actions

✅ EMPEZAR/COMENZAR A + INFINITIVE:

💡 Examples:
→ Empiezo a estudiar (I start studying)
→ Comenzó a llover (It started to rain)
→ Empezamos a trabajar (We start working)

⚡ Note: Preposition 'a' is required!

⚠️ DEJAR DE + INFINITIVE (to stop doing):

💡 Examples:
→ Dejé de fumar (I stopped smoking)
→ No dejes de llamarme (Don't stop calling me)
→ Dejamos de hablar (We stopped talking)

⚡ Note: Use 'de' not 'a'

💡 PARAR DE + INFINITIVE (to stop doing):

Similar to dejar de
→ Para de hablar (Stop talking)
→ No pares de correr (Don't stop running)

📍 Both dejar de and parar de mean 'to stop'

sections.subtitle: Obligation & Necessity
sections.content:
📋 Expressing Obligation

✅ TENER QUE + INFINITIVE (to have to):

💡 Personal obligation
→ Tengo que estudiar (I have to study)
→ Tienes que venir (You have to come)
→ Tenemos que salir (We have to leave)

🎯 Strongest form of obligation

⚠️ HAY QUE + INFINITIVE (one must):

💡 Impersonal/general obligation
→ Hay que estudiar (One must study)
→ Hay que llegar temprano (One must arrive early)
→ Hay que trabajar (It's necessary to work)

⚡ Only uses 'hay' form (no specific subject)

💡 DEBER + INFINITIVE (should/ought to):

💡 Moral obligation or advice
→ Debes estudiar (You should study)
→ Debemos ayudar (We ought to help)
→ Debo llamar (I should call)

🎯 Softer than tener que

📍 Strength: tener que > deber > hay que

sections.subtitle: Duration & Continuation
sections.content:
📋 Expressing Duration & Continuation

✅ LLEVAR + TIME + GERUND:

💡 Duration of ongoing action
→ Llevo tres años estudiando español
  (I've been studying Spanish for three years)
→ Lleva una hora esperando
  (He/She has been waiting for one hour)
→ Llevan dos meses trabajando aquí
  (They've been working here for two months)

⚡ Different from English:
Uses present tense (not present perfect)!

⚠️ SEGUIR/CONTINUAR + GERUND:

💡 Keep/continue doing
→ Sigo estudiando (I keep studying)
→ Continúa trabajando (He/She continues working)
→ Siguen viviendo aquí (They still live here)
→ Sigue lloviendo (It's still raining)

🎯 Uses:
• Express ongoing continuation
• Show action hasn't stopped
• Emphasize persistence

questions.question: What is the structure of the progressive form?
questions.hint: Use estar + -ando/-iendo form to express action in progress.

questions.question: 'Estoy comiendo' means...
questions.hint: Present progressive: action happening at this moment.

questions.question: 'Como a las 2' vs 'Estoy comiendo ahora' - What's the difference?

answers.text: Como = habitual action; Estoy comiendo = action in progress now
Como is past; Estoy comiendo is present
Como is formal; Estoy comiendo is informal

questions.hint: Present tense for habits; progressive for actions happening RIGHT NOW.

questions.question: How do you say 'I'm going to study'?
questions.hint: Use ir (present) + a + infinitive for immediate future/plans.

questions.question: 'Voy a comer' expresses...
questions.hint: Ir a + infinitive = going to do something (near future).

questions.question: How do you say 'I just ate'?
questions.hint: Use acabar de + infinitive for 'just did' something (recent past).

questions.question: 'Acaba de salir' means...
questions.hint: Acabar de + infinitive = just did something (immediate past).

questions.question: 'Vuelvo a intentar' means...
questions.hint: Volver a + infinitive = to do something again (repetition).

questions.question: 'Volvió a llamar' means...
questions.hint: Volver a + infinitive emphasizes repeating an action.

questions.question: 'Suelo desayunar a las 8' means...

answers.text: I want to have breakfast at 8

questions.hint: Soler + infinitive = usually do something (habitual action).

questions.question: What tenses can 'soler' be used in?
questions.hint: Soler is limited: suelo (present) and solía (imperfect) only.

questions.question: 'Empiezo a estudiar' means...

answers.text: I start to study / I'm starting to study

questions.hint: Empezar a + infinitive = to start doing something. Note preposition 'a'!

questions.question: Which preposition follows 'empezar/comenzar'?
questions.hint: Remember: empezar/comenzar A + infinitive (with 'a').

questions.question: 'Dejé de fumar' means...
questions.hint: Dejar de + infinitive = to stop doing something.

questions.question: Which preposition follows 'dejar' when it means 'to stop'?
questions.hint: Dejar DE + infinitive = stop doing. Use 'de' not 'a'.

questions.question: 'Tengo que estudiar' means...
questions.hint: Tener que + infinitive = personal obligation (have to).

questions.question: 'Hay que estudiar' means...

answers.text: One must study / It's necessary to study (impersonal)

questions.hint: Hay que + infinitive = impersonal obligation (one must, it's necessary).

questions.question: 'Tengo que' vs 'Hay que' - What's the difference?

answers.text: Tengo que = personal (I have to); Hay que = impersonal (one must)
Tengo que is past; Hay que is present

questions.hint: Tener que is personal; hay que is impersonal (no specific subject).

questions.question: 'Debes estudiar' means...
questions.hint: Deber + infinitive = should/ought to (softer than tener que).

questions.question: 'Llevo tres años estudiando español' means...

answers.text: I've been studying Spanish for three years
I will study Spanish for three years
I studied Spanish three years ago
I'm carrying three years of Spanish

questions.hint: Llevar + time + gerund = have been doing (duration). Uses present tense!

questions.question: 'Lleva una hora esperando' - What tense is 'lleva'?

answers.text: Present (Spanish uses present, not present perfect)

questions.hint: Unlike English 'has been waiting', Spanish uses present: lleva (carries).

questions.question: 'Sigo estudiando' means...
questions.hint: Seguir/continuar + gerund = to keep doing, continue doing.

questions.question: 'Sigue lloviendo' means...

answers.text: It's still raining / It keeps raining

questions.hint: Seguir + gerund emphasizes continuation: still doing/keeps doing.
